newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor mulls creation of seven units.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor mulls creation of seven units.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) plans to set up seven power-generating companies and sell them to the private sector as part of its privatisation programme, the state firm said.
Napocor president Guido A. Delgado said in documents officially released on Sunday that Napocor's power generation business would be taken over by the seven power-generating companies, or gencos.
Napocor will be broken up into four gencos serving the main island of Luzon and three gencos handling power generation for the central Visayas islands and the southern island of Mindanao.
Ownership of the gencos will then be offered to the private sector, Delgado said.
But power transmission will remain a state monopoly as interconnection of major grids still must be completed, he added.
Currently, Napocor controls the country's power generation and transmission business.
Delgado said privatisation of Napocor would depend on passage by Congress of an electricity sector restructuring bill.
The bill, which sets down guidelines for privatising the firm, will likely be passed within the year, he said.
